title: A name that is a standard term in other capitals or spacing is refused
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, working in {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Starting screen: the Credit Terms page (Settings, then "Credit Terms" in the Finance group) is open on the Active tab.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Click "New Credit Term".
  2. Type "net 30" in Name.
  3. Click the Days box.
  4. Replace the Name with "Net30".
  5. Click the Days box.
  6. Replace the Name with "due on receipt".
  7. Click the Days box.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the "New Credit Term" window opens.
  • Step 2: the Name reads net 30.
  • Step 3: the message "Net 30 is already a standard term. Pick another name." shows under Name, and "Create Credit Term" is disabled.
  • Step 4: the Name reads Net30.
  • Step 5: the same message shows: "Net 30 is already a standard term. Pick another name."
  • Step 6: the Name reads due on receipt.
  • Step 7: the message reads "Due on Receipt is already a standard term. Pick another name."

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11672 (Story 3, Create or edit a credit term)

  • S3-R9, a standard term's name: “Name matches a standard term ignoring capitals and spaces (for example "net 30" or "Net30"): "{Standard name} is already a standard term. Pick another name." (for example "Net 30 is already a standard term. Pick another name.")”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Name matches a standard term | "{name} is already a standard term. Pick another name." | Inline error, persists until corrected”
  • S3-R9: “Validation rules and their exact messages, shown under the field:”
  • Assumptions: “Stored customer and vendor terms carry inconsistent spellings from old imports and migrations (for example "NET 30" and "Due On Receipt"); every count, match and move treats names as equal when they differ only in capitals and spaces.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
